metaData.originalTitle: TencentDB Agent Memory 全球正式开源：让 Agent 沉淀经验，让人专注创造
metaData.title: TencentDB Agent Memory is Now Open Source Globally: Let Agents Accumulate Experience, Let Humans Focus on Creation
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tencent Cloud officially open-sources TencentDB Agent Memory, a layered memory engine for AI Agents. Using an L0-L3 layered architecture and context offloading technology, it reduces token consumption while improving task completion rates.
metaData.summary: Tencent Cloud Database team has officially open-sourced TencentDB Agent Memory, a layered memory engine under the MIT license. It aims to solve core problems AI Agents face in long-term tasks, such as broken cross-session memory, confusion between facts and preferences, and context bloat. The project proposes an L0-L3 four-layer memory architecture: Raw Conversation Layer, Atomic Memory Layer, Scenario Summarization Layer, and User Profile Layer, connected by an extraction-aggregation-distillation pipeline. Technically, it uses context offloading and Mermaid infinite canvas technology to move raw tool results and task structures to external files, keeping only summaries and indexes in the context, thus breaking the linear growth of tokens. Evaluation data shows that when integrated as an OpenClaw plugin, it can save up to 61.38% of tokens, relatively improve task pass rate by 51.52%, and increase long-term memory accuracy from 48% to 76%. The project supports two integration methods: OpenClaw and Hermes Gateway, offering one-command installation and Docker deployment.

mainPoints.point: TencentDB Agent Memory proposes an L0-L3 four-layer memory architecture to solve long-term Agent memory problems.
mainPoints.explanation: L0 retains all interactions, L1 automatically extracts atomic information like facts and preferences, L2 aggregates by task scenario, and L3 distills stable user profiles. Layers are connected via an extraction-aggregation-distillation pipeline, and each layer can be independently upgraded or replaced.

mainPoints.point: Context offloading and Mermaid infinite canvas technology break the bottleneck of linear token growth.
mainPoints.explanation: Raw tool results and task structures are offloaded to external files, with only summaries and indexes kept in the context. This prevents token consumption from growing linearly with task length while maintaining traceability of original text and navigability of structure.

mainPoints.point: Evaluation data validates the dual effect of reducing token usage and improving task completion rate.
mainPoints.explanation: In WideSearch evaluations, it saves 61.38% of tokens and improves pass rate by 51.52%. PersonaMem long-term memory accuracy increases from 48% to 76%. It converges stably on long-chain tasks like programming, research, and document analysis.

keyQuotes: Memory isn't about making AI remember everything; it's about freeing people from having to repeat everything.

Each layer does only one thing, and layers are connected by an extraction-aggregation-distillation pipeline. Any layer can be independently upgraded or replaced, so your Agent won't forget who you are just because a session changes.

We open-sourced TencentDB Agent Memory because we believe there is no standard answer for memory products. Rather than creating a perfect solution, we want to work with developers to make the product richer, more robust, and more usable.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: The Evolution of Agent/Skills/Teams Architectures and Principles of Technology Selection
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory of AI Agents from monolithic to multi-agent, then to Skills pluginization and Teams parallel collaboration, and, drawing on the latest research from Google and Anthropic, provides a scientific methodology for selection.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: 5 Lessons Learned from 400 Million Tokens: What Happened When 6 AI Agents Wrote Code for 4 Days Straight?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a four-day multi-agent automated programming experiment, this article reveals that 'glue code' and engineering stability are more challenging and critical than prompt design when building AI systems.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: From 7.9% to 54% Adoption: The Three-Stage Evolution of Kuaishou's Intelligent Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the three-generation architectural evolution of Kuaishou's intelligent code review system—from pure LLM heuristics to knowledge engine-driven, and finally to Agentic autonomous decision-making—increasing the CR adoption rate from 7.9% to 54%.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.
